newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries end flat to lower, await fresh data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries end flat to lower, await fresh data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ended flat to lower across the yield curve in extremely dull trading as players squared portfolios ahead of the weekend and braced for upcoming fresh data, analysts said.
The 30-year benchmark Treasury bond ended down 9/32 at 100-25/32. Its yield rose slightly to 6.44 percent.

"Activity today has been exceptionaly light. If players are doing anything, it's a little bit of position squaring ahead of the weekend," said John Cavanan, money market analyst at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"I think things will be at least more interesting than today as we go into next week, when new data will be released," Canavan added.

The market spent the entire session confined to very tight trading ranges as the market had a very tepid response to the only relevant piece of data released on Friday, the October import and export prices report.
The Labor Department said overall import prices rose 0.4 percent in October against a revised 1.1 percent jump in September. Export prices were down 0.3 percent against a 0.8 percent drop earlier.
"(The data) reminded us that low import prices have been one of the factors explaining all the good inflation reports," said Robert Dederick, chief economist at Northern Trust.
"All year long import prices, ex-oil, have barely moved ... and that also reflects the sluggish worldwide economy," Dederick added.

Recent consumer price index reports showed inflation in the U.S. remains tame. The latest figures available show CPI rose 0.3 percent overall in the month of November. The core index, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.2 percent in the same period.
The market was also somewhat disappointed Friday as the Federal Reserve refrained from carrying out an expected coupon pass operation.
Traders said the operation was expected after the flood of fresh supply that entered the market earlier in the week.
The Fed, however, decided to add temporary reserves to the banking system through $2.0 billion customer repurchase agreements.
"We were expecting the Fed to come in with a coupon pass to prop prices up, which didn't happen," said a trader at an investment bank. "The market was somewhat disappointed."
The market also paid little attention to remarks by Federal Reserve Board Governor Susan Philips on Friday.
Philips said she sees consumer spending rising in the fourth quarter, adding that her best guess is that the economy is to stay moderate but in a sustainable growth path.
Analysts said trading on Friday was in the hands of professional players. Hedge and mutual funds as well as retailers were mostly out of the market.
Volume was extremely thin. By late afternoon, total volume as measured by GovPX was $46.35 billion, around 20 percent below average for a Friday autumm.
Turnover in the bill sector was just under $9.0 billion, the lowest registered so far this year, including days when the market had abbreviated sessions.
GovPX publishes real-time Treasury prices and volume from five of the six intra-dealer brokers, representing 65 percent of the intra-dealers trades.
The three-month Treasury bill rate closed flat at 5.03 percent. The six-month bill rate was unchanged at 5.06 percent. The year bill rate was up one basis point at 5.15 percent.

The two-year note closed down 1/32 at 99-28/32, yielding 5.69 percent. The five-year note was flat at 99-24/32 to yield 5.93 percent. The ten-year note closed down 1/32 at 102-20/32, yielding 6.14 percent.
